jobs.title: Environmental Health Safety Specialist
jobs.description:
EHS Specialist I (Environmental, Health & Safety Specialist I)

Reports To:
EHS Manager
Position Summary
We are seeking an Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) Specialist I to support and maintain a safe, healthy, and environmentally compliant manufacturing workplace. This role is responsible for assisting with environmental, health, and safety programs, ensuring compliance with OSHA, EPA, and company standards while promoting a strong safety culture throughout the facility.
The ideal candidate is passionate about workplace safety, environmental stewardship, and continuous improvement. They will partner with employees, supervisors, contractors, and leadership to identify hazards, implement corrective actions, and support regulatory compliance across all manufacturing operations.
Please note that duties and responsibilities may change with or without notice.
Essential Responsibilities
Environmental Health & Safety
Perform daily safety inspections throughout production, laboratories, warehouse, shipping, and receiving areas.
Conduct weekly hazardous waste inspections of satellite accumulation areas and maintain hazardous waste manifests.
Perform monthly stormwater inspections and collect stormwater samples during required qualifying rain events.
Support hazardous waste minimization initiatives for thermoset and thermoplastic manufacturing operations.
Identify environmental, health, and safety risks and assist in implementing corrective actions.
Monitor and track corrective actions resulting from incident and accident investigations.
Observe workplace behaviors and address unsafe acts or conditions through coaching and corrective measures.
Promote safe work practices and ensure employees understand proper safety procedures.
Assist with Emergency Response Team (ERT) activities and Safety Committee meetings.
Help develop, revise, and maintain EHS policies, procedures, and documentation.
Conduct employee training on topics including Hazard Communication, Hazardous Waste Management, PPE, and other safety programs.
Promote environmental and safety awareness through formal training sessions and daily employee interaction.
Assist with the annual Hazardous Materials Business Plan (HMBP) updates.
Support industrial hygiene monitoring activities as needed.
Perform ergonomic assessments and recommend improvements.
Assist in developing and implementing EHS programs that comply with OSHA, EPA, and company requirements.
Support regulatory inspections, audits, and compliance initiatives.
Maintain accurate EHS records and documentation.
Participate in continuous improvement initiatives related to workplace safety and environmental performance.

Qualifications
Education
High school diploma or GED required.
Associate degree in Environmental Health & Safety, Occupational Safety, Environmental Science, or a related field preferred.

Experience
Minimum of one (1) year of Environmental, Health & Safety experience.
Manufacturing experience preferred.
Experience in composites or industrial manufacturing environments is a plus.

Knowledge & Skills
Working knowledge of OSHA, EPA, and applicable environmental and safety regulations.
Familiarity with:
Hazardous Waste Management
Hazardous Materials Business Plan (HMBP)
Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP)
Industrial Hygiene
Hazard Communication (HazCom)
Basic understanding of Local, State, and Federal regulatory requirements.
Knowledge of electrical and high-voltage safety practices is preferred.
Experience supporting emergency preparedness and incident response programs.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to build professional relationships across all levels of the organization.
Strong organizational, problem-solving, and time management skills.
Ability to prioritize multiple projects in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
Proficient with Microsoft Office applications.

Physical Requirements
Frequently walk throughout the manufacturing facility.
Stand, bend, reach, climb, and lift throughout the workday.
Occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.
Wear required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) in designated production areas.
Work safely around manufacturing equipment, chemicals, and industrial processes.

Preferred Qualifications
Associate degree or higher in Environmental Health & Safety or a related discipline.
Experience conducting safety training and employee engagement programs.
Experience with accident investigations and root cause analysis.
Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, 5S, or continuous improvement methodologies.
OSHA 30 certification or similar EHS certification is a plus.

jobs.company: NSW Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure
jobs.title: Environmental Assessment Officer
jobs.location: Harris Park, New South Wales, Australia
jobs.description:
Build your future with the team driving NSW communities, spaces and economies

Shape NSW's future through major project assessment and community outcomes.

Permanent full-time opportunity,

Office location based in Parramatta with flexible working supported

Salary relative to experience, and ranges from $119,329 to $134,463 + super

Join our team and shape your world in a workplace that empowers you to do your best work and build a meaningful career. In this role, you will contribute to shaping lives and communities across NSW, while shaping your own career. You will enjoy flexible work options, varied and impactful projects, and a vibrant, diverse team culture built on collaboration, inclusion and support. We are creating a workplace where everyone belongs and where you can balance work, life and wellbeing.

The role

As an Environmental Assessment Officer
in the Industry Assessment team, you will assess major projects across a wide range of interesting and dynamic sectors that help shape communities, support economic growth and deliver critical infrastructure across NSW. You'll provide expert planning advice that balances community expectations, government priorities and statutory requirements while helping drive better planning outcomes.

Working across a range of projects, you'll analyse complex information, prepare clear recommendations and engage with stakeholders to help deliver better outcomes for the state. This is a rewarding opportunity to make a real impact while shaping thriving and connected communities.

For more information about this position, read the full Role Description: Environmental Assessment Officer

What you will bring to the role

Ability to assess the merits of State significant projects quickly and effectively in sectors such as manufacturing and chemical industries, renewable fuels, the circular economy including large scale waste and recycling, data centres, agricultural and aquaculture, warehouse and distribution facilities, including within the Western Sydney Aerotropolis and State activation precincts.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to translate complex technical information into clear, concise and accessible advice, reports and recommendations for diverse audiences.
Strong problem-solving and analytical skills with the ability to research, evaluate complex issues and develop practical solutions to support sound environmental assessment outcomes.
Outstanding stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to build effective relationships, manage competing expectations and work collaboratively with government agencies, industry representatives, developers and community stakeholders
Demonstrated ability to prioritise competing workloads, manage multiple projects and deliver high-quality outcomes within demanding timeframes in a fast-paced environment.

What is an essential requirement:

Degree in environmental science or management, engineering, planning or other relevant discipline
Willingness to travel and (minimum) Class C Driver’s License.

About Us

At the Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure (DPHI), you could shape your world while helping us shape the future of NSW. Together, we create vibrant communities, places and precincts, and manage land, assets and property.
(We are a high-performing organisation that proudly reflects the communities we serve. Our diversity strengthens our cultural capability and enables us to make a meaningful difference in the lives of people across NSW. As an inclusive and accessible workplace, we value your contribution, lived experience and cultural knowledge, and we want you to feel supported, connected and empowered to succeed. With flexible work arrangements, job share options, workplace adjustments and various employee affinity groups, we are here to help you thrive every day.
Join us

If this role sounds like the right fit for you, we encourage you to apply with your CV and cover letter. We’d love to hear from you and explore how you can shape your world with us. Applications close Sunday 16 Aug 2026 at 11:55pm
. Should you require further information about the role please contact Catriona Shirley (catriona.shirley@dpie.nsw.gov.au)

A talent pool may be created for ongoing and temporary opportunities of the same role or role type that may become available over the next 18 months.

Check out our Aboriginal applicants guide to assist with applying for the role or contact our Aboriginal Career pathways team for a yarn.
We encourage and support applications from people with disability. Please reach out to us to discuss any accommodations or adjustments that may be needed during the recruitment process, ensuring that you have every opportunity to showcase your talent, skills, and potential. Contact the Talent Team via talent.acquisition@dpie.nsw.gov.au or (02) 63637676​ - HR Support, option 2, DPHI People Advisory, option 1 and reference 'Request an Adjustment - Job Title and Reference Number'.
Please note to be eligible to apply for this position you must be an Australian or New Zealand citizen or permanent resident or hold a valid Australian working Visa for the duration of the appointment. This role is subject to standard pre-employment checks, including a criminal record check.

jobs.title: Senior Air Quality Consultant
jobs.description:
As part of continued growth of our Air Quality team, ERM has a position available for an experienced Senior Consultant to join our national team.

ERM is a global environmental consultancy with one of the largest group of air quality specialists in Australia. We have a client base comprising major Australian and international companies, as well as federal and state government departments. Our projects (in Australia and overseas) include impact assessment and mitigation, air quality monitoring, air quality assessment, dispersion modelling, odour and dust assessment, emissions inventory development, carbon management, applied meteorology, and regulatory reporting.

You will be part of a growing dynamic international company that clients trust and choose to engage. ERM offers a structured career path with outstanding opportunities. If you are a highly motivated and results-orientated person looking to make your mark in a leading environmental consultancy, then we would like to hear from you!

This is an excellent career opportunity for a senior-level professional looking to advance their career with a global environmental leader, and to make a significant impact in successfully implementing ERM's global strategy.

Role Responsibilities:

Deliver emission estimation inventories, odour and air quality modelling assessments;
Write technical environmental reports, effective proposals, and tenders;
Plan projects with a range of complexity and scale;
Achieve client’s expectations for scope, budget, schedule, and quality;
Lead client-focused air permitting and compliance strategies for industrial facilities, addressing complex regulatory and technical issues while maintaining strong client relationships and supporting operational flexibility;
Develop and expand client relationships that support repeat business, identifying and developing new opportunities;
Capitalize on existing client relationships to expand ERM’s profile and market share in the regional air quality market (through a combination of excellence in technical delivery and business development);
Mentor team members in the proper planning and execution of air quality projects, and conduct independent technical reviews of deliverable work products;
Support the general growth and development of ERM’s global air quality services;
Collaborate with other ERM global practitioners to execute air quality projects.

Requirements:

BS/MS in engineering (chemical, mechanical, environmental), environmental science, or related degree.
8+ years of relevant experience in air quality/compliance consulting.
Well established reputation and recognized technical expertise by the marketplace.
Proven experience completing emission inventories and air quality modelling assessments.
Technical expertise such as WRF modelling, RStudio programming is desirable.
Proven experience in business development for large air quality/regulatory compliance contracts, with the ability to contribute to ERM’s annual sales goals.
Excellent communication (written/verbal), strategic thinking, negotiation, presentation, and “people” skills.
Positive outlook, collaborative, and driven by the success of ERM as a global company.
Authorisation to work in Australia.

Who We Are:

As the world’s leading sustainability consulting firm, ERM is uniquely positioned to contribute to the environment and society through the expertise and energy of our employees worldwide. Sustainability is what we do and is at the heart of both our service offerings and how we operate our business. For our people, our vision means attracting, inspiring, developing and rewarding our people to work with the best clients and on the biggest challenges, thus creating valuable careers. We achieve our vision in a sustainable manner by maintaining and living our ERM beliefs that include Together we Challenge, Expertise is our Superpower, and Impact Ignites us.

ERM does not accept recruiting agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to our job’s alias, ERM employees or any other company location. ERM is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

Thank you for your interest in ERM.

new_jobs.title: Environmental Health Safety Specialist
new_jobs.description:
EHS Specialist I (Environmental, Health & Safety Specialist I)

Reports To:
EHS Manager
Position Summary
We are seeking an Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) Specialist I to support and maintain a safe, healthy, and environmentally compliant manufacturing workplace. This role is responsible for assisting with environmental, health, and safety programs, ensuring compliance with OSHA, EPA, and company standards while promoting a strong safety culture throughout the facility.
The ideal candidate is passionate about workplace safety, environmental stewardship, and continuous improvement. They will partner with employees, supervisors, contractors, and leadership to identify hazards, implement corrective actions, and support regulatory compliance across all manufacturing operations.
Please note that duties and responsibilities may change with or without notice.
Essential Responsibilities
Environmental Health & Safety
Perform daily safety inspections throughout production, laboratories, warehouse, shipping, and receiving areas.
Conduct weekly hazardous waste inspections of satellite accumulation areas and maintain hazardous waste manifests.
Perform monthly stormwater inspections and collect stormwater samples during required qualifying rain events.
Support hazardous waste minimization initiatives for thermoset and thermoplastic manufacturing operations.
Identify environmental, health, and safety risks and assist in implementing corrective actions.
Monitor and track corrective actions resulting from incident and accident investigations.
Observe workplace behaviors and address unsafe acts or conditions through coaching and corrective measures.
Promote safe work practices and ensure employees understand proper safety procedures.
Assist with Emergency Response Team (ERT) activities and Safety Committee meetings.
Help develop, revise, and maintain EHS policies, procedures, and documentation.
Conduct employee training on topics including Hazard Communication, Hazardous Waste Management, PPE, and other safety programs.
Promote environmental and safety awareness through formal training sessions and daily employee interaction.
Assist with the annual Hazardous Materials Business Plan (HMBP) updates.
Support industrial hygiene monitoring activities as needed.
Perform ergonomic assessments and recommend improvements.
Assist in developing and implementing EHS programs that comply with OSHA, EPA, and company requirements.
Support regulatory inspections, audits, and compliance initiatives.
Maintain accurate EHS records and documentation.
Participate in continuous improvement initiatives related to workplace safety and environmental performance.

Qualifications
Education
High school diploma or GED required.
Associate degree in Environmental Health & Safety, Occupational Safety, Environmental Science, or a related field preferred.

Experience
Minimum of one (1) year of Environmental, Health & Safety experience.
Manufacturing experience preferred.
Experience in composites or industrial manufacturing environments is a plus.

Knowledge & Skills
Working knowledge of OSHA, EPA, and applicable environmental and safety regulations.
Familiarity with:
Hazardous Waste Management
Hazardous Materials Business Plan (HMBP)
Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP)
Industrial Hygiene
Hazard Communication (HazCom)
Basic understanding of Local, State, and Federal regulatory requirements.
Knowledge of electrical and high-voltage safety practices is preferred.
Experience supporting emergency preparedness and incident response programs.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to build professional relationships across all levels of the organization.
Strong organizational, problem-solving, and time management skills.
Ability to prioritize multiple projects in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
Proficient with Microsoft Office applications.

Physical Requirements
Frequently walk throughout the manufacturing facility.
Stand, bend, reach, climb, and lift throughout the workday.
Occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.
Wear required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) in designated production areas.
Work safely around manufacturing equipment, chemicals, and industrial processes.

Preferred Qualifications
Associate degree or higher in Environmental Health & Safety or a related discipline.
Experience conducting safety training and employee engagement programs.
Experience with accident investigations and root cause analysis.
Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, 5S, or continuous improvement methodologies.
OSHA 30 certification or similar EHS certification is a plus.

new_jobs.title: Environmental Assessment Officer
new_jobs.location: Harris Park, New South Wales, Australia
new_jobs.description:
Build your future with the team driving NSW communities, spaces and economies

Shape NSW's future through major project assessment and community outcomes.

Permanent full-time opportunity,

Office location based in Parramatta with flexible working supported

Salary relative to experience, and ranges from $119,329 to $134,463 + super

Join our team and shape your world in a workplace that empowers you to do your best work and build a meaningful career. In this role, you will contribute to shaping lives and communities across NSW, while shaping your own career. You will enjoy flexible work options, varied and impactful projects, and a vibrant, diverse team culture built on collaboration, inclusion and support. We are creating a workplace where everyone belongs and where you can balance work, life and wellbeing.

The role

As an Environmental Assessment Officer
in the Industry Assessment team, you will assess major projects across a wide range of interesting and dynamic sectors that help shape communities, support economic growth and deliver critical infrastructure across NSW. You'll provide expert planning advice that balances community expectations, government priorities and statutory requirements while helping drive better planning outcomes.

Working across a range of projects, you'll analyse complex information, prepare clear recommendations and engage with stakeholders to help deliver better outcomes for the state. This is a rewarding opportunity to make a real impact while shaping thriving and connected communities.

For more information about this position, read the full Role Description: Environmental Assessment Officer

What you will bring to the role

Ability to assess the merits of State significant projects quickly and effectively in sectors such as manufacturing and chemical industries, renewable fuels, the circular economy including large scale waste and recycling, data centres, agricultural and aquaculture, warehouse and distribution facilities, including within the Western Sydney Aerotropolis and State activation precincts.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to translate complex technical information into clear, concise and accessible advice, reports and recommendations for diverse audiences.
Strong problem-solving and analytical skills with the ability to research, evaluate complex issues and develop practical solutions to support sound environmental assessment outcomes.
Outstanding stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to build effective relationships, manage competing expectations and work collaboratively with government agencies, industry representatives, developers and community stakeholders
Demonstrated ability to prioritise competing workloads, manage multiple projects and deliver high-quality outcomes within demanding timeframes in a fast-paced environment.

What is an essential requirement:

Degree in environmental science or management, engineering, planning or other relevant discipline
Willingness to travel and (minimum) Class C Driver’s License.

About Us

At the Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure (DPHI), you could shape your world while helping us shape the future of NSW. Together, we create vibrant communities, places and precincts, and manage land, assets and property.
(We are a high-performing organisation that proudly reflects the communities we serve. Our diversity strengthens our cultural capability and enables us to make a meaningful difference in the lives of people across NSW. As an inclusive and accessible workplace, we value your contribution, lived experience and cultural knowledge, and we want you to feel supported, connected and empowered to succeed. With flexible work arrangements, job share options, workplace adjustments and various employee affinity groups, we are here to help you thrive every day.
Join us

If this role sounds like the right fit for you, we encourage you to apply with your CV and cover letter. We’d love to hear from you and explore how you can shape your world with us. Applications close Sunday 16 Aug 2026 at 11:55pm
. Should you require further information about the role please contact Catriona Shirley (catriona.shirley@dpie.nsw.gov.au)

A talent pool may be created for ongoing and temporary opportunities of the same role or role type that may become available over the next 18 months.

Check out our Aboriginal applicants guide to assist with applying for the role or contact our Aboriginal Career pathways team for a yarn.
We encourage and support applications from people with disability. Please reach out to us to discuss any accommodations or adjustments that may be needed during the recruitment process, ensuring that you have every opportunity to showcase your talent, skills, and potential. Contact the Talent Team via talent.acquisition@dpie.nsw.gov.au or (02) 63637676​ - HR Support, option 2, DPHI People Advisory, option 1 and reference 'Request an Adjustment - Job Title and Reference Number'.
Please note to be eligible to apply for this position you must be an Australian or New Zealand citizen or permanent resident or hold a valid Australian working Visa for the duration of the appointment. This role is subject to standard pre-employment checks, including a criminal record check.

new_jobs.title: Senior Air Quality Consultant
new_jobs.description:
As part of continued growth of our Air Quality team, ERM has a position available for an experienced Senior Consultant to join our national team.

ERM is a global environmental consultancy with one of the largest group of air quality specialists in Australia. We have a client base comprising major Australian and international companies, as well as federal and state government departments. Our projects (in Australia and overseas) include impact assessment and mitigation, air quality monitoring, air quality assessment, dispersion modelling, odour and dust assessment, emissions inventory development, carbon management, applied meteorology, and regulatory reporting.

You will be part of a growing dynamic international company that clients trust and choose to engage. ERM offers a structured career path with outstanding opportunities. If you are a highly motivated and results-orientated person looking to make your mark in a leading environmental consultancy, then we would like to hear from you!

This is an excellent career opportunity for a senior-level professional looking to advance their career with a global environmental leader, and to make a significant impact in successfully implementing ERM's global strategy.

Role Responsibilities:

Deliver emission estimation inventories, odour and air quality modelling assessments;
Write technical environmental reports, effective proposals, and tenders;
Plan projects with a range of complexity and scale;
Achieve client’s expectations for scope, budget, schedule, and quality;
Lead client-focused air permitting and compliance strategies for industrial facilities, addressing complex regulatory and technical issues while maintaining strong client relationships and supporting operational flexibility;
Develop and expand client relationships that support repeat business, identifying and developing new opportunities;
Capitalize on existing client relationships to expand ERM’s profile and market share in the regional air quality market (through a combination of excellence in technical delivery and business development);
Mentor team members in the proper planning and execution of air quality projects, and conduct independent technical reviews of deliverable work products;
Support the general growth and development of ERM’s global air quality services;
Collaborate with other ERM global practitioners to execute air quality projects.

Requirements:

BS/MS in engineering (chemical, mechanical, environmental), environmental science, or related degree.
8+ years of relevant experience in air quality/compliance consulting.
Well established reputation and recognized technical expertise by the marketplace.
Proven experience completing emission inventories and air quality modelling assessments.
Technical expertise such as WRF modelling, RStudio programming is desirable.
Proven experience in business development for large air quality/regulatory compliance contracts, with the ability to contribute to ERM’s annual sales goals.
Excellent communication (written/verbal), strategic thinking, negotiation, presentation, and “people” skills.
Positive outlook, collaborative, and driven by the success of ERM as a global company.
Authorisation to work in Australia.
